problem: Existing LLM-based VLN methods lose information when converting vision to text, rely on rigid prompts or manually designed reasoning steps, and have weak closed-loop control, so errors accumulate along the trajectory.
motivation: LLMs bring strong reasoning and generalization to VLN, but hand-designed reasoning templates and open-loop decisions limit robustness in unseen environments. The paper argues that autonomous CoT reasoning with closed-loop feedback use and online error correction is needed, while cloud LLM calls must stay cost-controlled.
key_idea: Fine-tune an open-source LLM for VLN with three-stage SFT, then optimize its closed-loop policy with RL for autonomous CoT and error correction, and let the lightweight local agent query a stronger cloud LLM only under high uncertainty.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract claims that RL after SFT encourages feedback use and error correction without predefined reasoning templates, and that selective cloud querying balances performance and compute cost.
method: Three-stage supervised fine-tuning: adapts an open-source LLM to VLN (the specific stages are not detailed in the abstract).
RL closed-loop policy optimization: further optimizes the policy with reinforcement learning to encourage robust use of feedback and online error correction, without predefined reasoning templates.
Autonomous chain-of-thought reasoning: the agent generates its own reasoning instead of following manually designed reasoning steps.
API-based collaborative reasoning module: a lightweight local agent selectively queries a stronger cloud LLM under high uncertainty to balance performance and computational cost.

setting.backbone: open-source LLM (unspecified) fine-tuned with SFT + RL; stronger cloud LLM via API for collaborative reasoning
setting.training_data: not specified in the abstract (three-stage SFT followed by RL on VLN data)
setting.simulator: not specified in the abstract (R2R, RxR, REVERIE benchmarks)

results: The abstract states that on R2R, RxR and REVERIE, DeepVLN achieves competitive or superior results to strong VLN-specific and LLM-based baselines, with higher success rates and path efficiency in most settings. No numbers are given.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so quantitative results and ablations could not be checked.
The collaborative module depends on a cloud LLM API, which adds cost and latency and requires network access.
